CHEMICALS AND PIGMENTS DEPARTMENT

Dear "Freon" Products Customers:

As I mentioned in my letter of January 25, 1989, today Du Pont is announcing another technological breakthrough resulting from our alternative development efforts.

Two Du Pont scientists, Helen A. Connon at the Chestnut Run Applications Research Center, and Donald B. Bivens at the Chambers Works Research Center, have developed patented technology for three-component refrigerant blends of environmentally acceptable (very low ozone depletion potential) compounds. The new technology will be tested in end use applications over the next few years. If successful, the new blends could lead to lower energy consumption and would require a minimum number of equipment changes. The result could be a more rapid transition from CFCs now used to service existing refrigeration and air conditioning equipment.

This technology offers significant advantages over other blend technology since desirable characteristics are maintained even if the refrigerant leaks from the system. In the event of a leak these blends continue to exhibit vapor pressure characteristics similar to CFC-12 and if the blends contain a flammable component the mixture will not become flammable.

Additional favorable characteristics of the new blends include:

(1) Energy efficiency and capacity can be improved relative to HFC-134a and should be comparable to that of CFC-12; and
(2) Oil solubility/lubricity can be improved relative to HFC-134a; some current refrigerant oils can be used.

Possible uses for the new blends include medium temperature food display cases, vending machines, water coolers, home refrigerators and freezers and automobile air conditioners.
